raw_case_text: A 28-year-old woman, pregnant, black, housekeeper, from Sao Francisco do Itabapoana, RJ, was admitted to the hospital on June 29th 2016, presenting weakness in the lower limbs and a consequent inability to ambulate for the previous week. The patient affirmed not having experienced similar episodes previously and claimed to be free of comorbidities. The patient reported rash on her limbs, pruritus and vomiting approximately 1 month before admission to the hospital. Initial obstetric examinations showed globular abdomen, unlimited uterus and absence of vaginal bleeding. The fetal heartbeat was not detected in the Sonar Doppler. Transvaginal ultrasonography evidenced a single fetus with longitudinal status and cephalic circumference suggesting 15 weeks of gestational age, normohydramnios, lack of heartbeat, and non-apparent active movements, which lead to the diagnosis of death and retained fetus (stillbirth). The patient was admitted to curettage and remained in hospital for 30 days. Analysis of the cerebrospinal fluid obtained by lumbar puncture and exams of the patient's peripheral blood revealed normal parameters (Table S1). The IgM serology for Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika, Epstein Barr and Cytomegalovirus were non-reactive (in further sections of this paper, diagnosis of ZIKV infection was confirmed by specific staining in placental and fetal tissues). The patient evolved to ascending and symmetrical flaccid tetraparesis, paresthesia, areflexia, presenting hands with pendular movement, dysautonomia (resting tachycardia and hypertension) and signs of respiratory insufficiency (mild dyspnea at rest which worsens upon effort), characterizing the GBS. The patient was further treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (30 g/day) for five days, atenolol 50 mg 12/12 h, amlodipine 5 mg 24 h, motor rehabilitation, respiratory physiotherapy and psychological intervention. In the second week of disease evolution, the neurological examination showed symmetric flaccid tetraparesis, motor incoordination, global areflexia and sensitive disorders (tactile and thermal distal hypoesthesia). Neurological follow up during and after the hospitalization period are described in Table S2. During the fourth week of disease progress, the patient was admitted to electroneuromyography, which revealed peripheral, acquired, chronic, symmetrical, diffuse, myelin and axonal (predominantly myelin), sensory and motor polyneuropathy: a condition that affected the peripheral nerves of the upper and lower limbs. In addition to that, the patient showed signs of neurogenic myopathy and muscular denervation. Together, these findings were compatible with polyradiculoneuropathy. By the end of the fourth week, the patient was discharged from the hospital under prescription of antihypertensive drugs and still being followed up by motor physical therapy. After 40 days of hospital discharge, the patient was orthostatic, walking-dependent for small distances and with pain sequels in the lower limbs. Five months later, residual sequels were still present with autonomous difficult scarvant gait. After 12 months, the gait patterns were regular; however, the speed and execution of upward and downward movements remained affected. Finally, the patient returned to her daily activities. Methods performed in this work using the placenta and fetal organs are described in Supplementary Material.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old pregnant Black woman presented with a 1-week history of bilateral lower limb weakness and inability to ambulate.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Approximately 1 month prior to admission on June 29, 2016, the patient experienced a rash on her limbs, pruritus, and vomiting. One week before admission, she developed progressive lower limb weakness resulting in an inability to walk. During hospitalization (following diagnosis of a 15-week intrauterine fetal demise and uterine curettage), she progressed to ascending symmetrical flaccid tetraparesis, paresthesia, global areflexia, pendular hand movements, dysautonomia (resting tachycardia and hypertension), and mild resting dyspnea worsening on exertion.
subjective.past_medical_history: 28-year-old Black pregnant woman working as a housekeeper in Sao Francisco do Itabapoana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Denied prior similar neurological episodes or medical comorbidities.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for lower limb weakness, inability to walk, subsequent ascending upper limb weakness, paresthesia, mild dyspnea at rest worsening on exertion, and prior limb rash, pruritus, and vomiting; negative for vaginal bleeding.

objective.physical_examination: Initial obstetric examination: globular abdomen, uterine size consistent with dates, no vaginal bleeding, and absent fetal heartbeat on Sonar Doppler. Neurological evolution during hospitalization: ascending and symmetrical flaccid tetraparesis, global areflexia, hands with pendular movement, motor incoordination, distal tactile and thermal hypoesthesia, dysautonomia (resting tachycardia and hypertension), and mild dyspnea at rest worsening on exertion.
objective.routine_investigations: Peripheral blood examinations: normal parameters. Transvaginal ultrasonography: single fetus in longitudinal lie with cephalic circumference corresponding to 15 weeks gestational age, normohydramnios, absent cardiac activity, and absent active fetal movements (confirming intrauterine fetal death / stillbirth). Maternal IgM serologies for dengue, chikungunya, Zika, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and cytomegalovirus (CMV): non-reactive.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture / cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis: normal parameters. Electroneuromyography (week 4 of illness): peripheral, acquired, chronic, symmetrical, diffuse mixed demyelinating and axonal (predominantly myelin) sensory and motor polyradiculoneuropathy affecting upper and lower limb peripheral nerves, accompanied by signs of neurogenic myopathy and muscular denervation. Placental and fetal tissue histopathology / immunostaining: positive specific staining confirming Zika virus (ZIKV) infection.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Maternal Zika virus (ZIKV) infection complicated by 15-week intrauterine fetal demise (stillbirth) and Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS; predominantly demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy with dysautonomia). Dengue, chikungunya, EBV, and CMV were excluded by negative IgM serologies. Confirmation: Specific ZIKV immunostaining in placental and fetal tissues coupled with characteristic clinical progression and electroneuromyographic confirmation of predominantly demyelinating sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy. Management and outcome: Underwent uterine curettage for retained stillbirth and received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG 30 g/day for 5 days), atenolol 50 mg every 12 hours, amlodipine 5 mg daily, motor rehabilitation, respiratory physiotherapy, and psychological support during a 30-day hospitalization. Discharged on antihypertensives and outpatient motor physical therapy; walked short distances with assistance at 40 days post-discharge, exhibited residual steppage/scarvant gait at 5 months, regained regular gait pattern at 12 months, and ultimately returned to daily activities.
